shared_context.topic: whether antibiotics prevent progression of Lyme disease

snippets.output: Antibiotics are effective in preventing the progression of Lyme disease if administered early in the course of the infection; early treatment of Lyme disease typically involves oral antibiotics such as doxycycline, amoxicillin, and cefuroxime axetil.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration: effectiveness statement + treatment modality + list of specific oral antibiotics as parallel properties of early Lyme treatment.

snippets.output: For early localized and early disseminated Lyme disease, a 10- to 21-day course of antibiotics is generally recommended.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel recommendation applying same antibiotic course to two stages of early Lyme disease.

snippets.output: If Lyme disease is treated promptly, most patients recover completely without long-term complications.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single-atom standalone fact about prognosis with prompt treatment.

snippets.output: If Lyme disease is not treated in its early stages, it can progress to more severe forms, including Lyme arthritis, neurological Lyme disease, and Lyme carditis. In such cases of Lyme disease, longer courses of antibiotics or intravenous antibiotics may be required.
snippets.pattern_notes: Conditional/causal chain: untreated -> progression to severe forms -> requires longer/IV antibiotics, with enumerated severe forms.
